steps.intent: Our primary objectives are to strictly limit the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism to a six-month renewal requiring a fresh Council decision for any further extension, to decisively shift humanitarian delivery toward cross-line modalities under Syrian sovereign control, and to expand funding for early recovery projects including basic electricity infrastructure. The main points of contention will be Western resistance to a firm six-month limit—as the P3 and humanitarian co-penholders strongly demand a full twelve-month mandate—and their vehement opposition to any language addressing the devastating impact of unilateral sanctions on Syrian humanitarian conditions.

messages.Albania: Albania firmly supports the humanitarian mandate and echoes the Secretary-General's unequivocal call for a full 12-month renewal to provide humanitarian actors with the necessary operational certainty and planning horizon. A six-month authorization, especially entering the harsh winter period, risks disrupting critical life-saving assistance to over four million people in northwest Syria. Furthermore, the inclusion of divisive, politicized language regarding unilateral coercive measures is unacceptable and distracts from the Council's primary duty to save lives.
messages.Brazil: Brazil remains deeply committed to addressing the dire humanitarian needs of the Syrian people in a strictly depoliticized manner. A 12-month authorization is vital to ensure humanitarian organizations have the predictability and stability required to plan and deliver life-saving assistance, particularly through the harsh winter months. We urge the penholder and all Council members to bridge existing divisions and prioritize Council unity so that uninterrupted humanitarian access is safeguarded.
messages.China: China commends the Russian Federation for putting forward this balanced and realistic draft resolution, which we fully support. The text rightly underscores full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria, the need to transition towards cross-line humanitarian delivery, and the critical importance of advancing early recovery projects across all sectors, including electricity. Furthermore, we strongly welcome the inclusion of language addressing the severe humanitarian harm caused by unilateral coercive measures, and China stands ready to vote in favour of the draft as presented.
messages.France: France cannot accept this draft as currently formulated. A full 12-month extension of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism is indispensable to ensure humanitarian predictability and avoid leaving millions of vulnerable Syrians without vital aid in the middle of winter. Moreover, the references to unilateral coercive measures are completely unacceptable, as targeted sanctions contain robust humanitarian exemptions and must not be instrumentalized to distract from the Syrian regime's own obstruction of aid.
messages.Gabon: Gabon emphasizes that addressing the critical humanitarian needs of the Syrian people must remain our absolute priority, free from political divisions. We support the expansion of early recovery projects and cross-line deliveries alongside the cross-border mechanism, which remains vital for millions of civilians. We urge the penholder to bridge differences on the duration and contentious language so the Council can adopt a compromise resolution by consensus before the mandate expires.
messages.Ghana: Ghana believes the Council must prioritize the urgent and lifesaving humanitarian needs of millions of vulnerable civilians across Syria. A six-month authorization creates severe operational uncertainty for humanitarian agencies, especially as the mandate would expire in the middle of winter; we therefore strongly urge a full twelve-month renewal. We also appeal to the penholder to remove polarizing language to preserve Council unity and ensure uninterrupted cross-border and cross-line aid delivery.
messages.India: India welcomes the draft's strong emphasis on early recovery projects, cross-line deliveries, and respect for Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity. However, to ensure operational predictability and avert a humanitarian cliff edge during the harsh winter months, we urge aligning the extension modalities with the compromise established under resolution 2585 (2021). We encourage all Council members to bridge differences through consensus so that uninterrupted, non-politicized humanitarian assistance reaches all Syrians in need.
messages.Ireland: As humanitarian co-penholder alongside Norway, Ireland underscores that our sole focus must remain meeting the critical, life-saving needs of over four million Syrians in the north-west. A full 12-month mandate extension is essential to provide humanitarian agencies with the necessary operational certainty, procurement lead times, and logistical stability to avoid an catastrophic winter cliff-edge. Contentious political elements, particularly language on unilateral coercive measures, distract from our core humanitarian mandate and must be removed to achieve consensus.
messages.Kenya: Kenya remains guided by the imperative to alleviate the suffering of the Syrian people and ensure predictable, unhindered humanitarian access across all modalities, including cross-border and cross-line. We urge the penholder to extend the authorization for 12 months, in line with the clear call of the Secretary-General and humanitarian agencies on the ground, which is vital for operational planning and upcoming winterization efforts. We also urge members to avoid divisive elements, including unilateral coercive measures, so that the Council can unite behind a consensus text that places the needs of the Syrian people above political differences.
messages.Mexico: Mexico reiterates that discussions on this resolution must remain strictly centered on meeting the urgent humanitarian needs of the Syrian people. Humanitarian agencies require predictability and operational certainty, which necessitates a full 12-month renewal of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism rather than an arrangement that creates uncertainty in mid-winter. We also encourage the penholder to remove divisive language regarding unilateral coercive measures in order to preserve Council unity and safeguard humanitarian access.
messages.Norway: As humanitarian co-penholder alongside Ireland, Norway's overriding priority is ensuring predictable, unhindered life-saving aid to more than 4 million people in north-west Syria. A 12-month extension is an operational necessity for the United Nations and humanitarian partners to effectively procure and deliver supplies ahead of the critical winter period. We cannot accept a six-month mandate conditioned on a subsequent resolution, nor the inclusion of contentious language regarding unilateral coercive measures in a purely humanitarian resolution.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates appreciates the Russian Federation's initiative and welcomes the strong emphasis on early recovery projects, including electricity, as well as the enhancement of cross-line aid deliveries, which are vital for meeting the needs of the Syrian people. To ensure this Council reaches the necessary consensus and avoids a lapse in humanitarian assistance, we encourage bridging differences on the duration and renewal mechanism to provide predictability for humanitarian actors. We also suggest calibrating the text regarding unilateral measures toward agreed compromise language that focuses squarely on safeguarding humanitarian operations and early recovery efforts.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom cannot support a text that severely undermines humanitarian operations by limiting the mandate to six months, expiring in the depths of winter when millions of vulnerable Syrians are in greatest need. Furthermore, language on unilateral coercive measures is entirely unacceptable; UK and allied sanctions target human rights abusers and contain clear humanitarian exemptions. Council action must be guided by objective humanitarian assessments, and we urge support for a straightforward 12-month renewal as put forward by the humanitarian co-penholders, Ireland and Norway.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support this draft as written. A clean 12-month reauthorization is an absolute humanitarian imperative to ensure humanitarians can effectively plan, procure, and deliver lifesaving assistance through the grueling winter months without Council-created uncertainty. Moreover, we categorically reject the politicized and baseless language regarding unilateral coercive measures, which contain robust humanitarian exemptions and are not the cause of the Syrian people's suffering.

In the interest of Council unity and humanitarian continuity, contentious references to unilateral coercive measures in PP6 and OP5 have been deleted. The draft firmly protects key priorities regarding Syrian sovereignty, the expansion of cross-line deliveries, and robust support for early recovery projects, including electricity.

messages.Albania: Albania maintains that a straightforward 12-month renewal of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism is indispensable to provide humanitarian actors the predictability required to save lives, particularly ahead of the harsh winter months. A six-month authorization severely undermines operational planning and leaves over four million vulnerable Syrians in unacceptable uncertainty. We urge the penholder to align the text with the clear appeals of the Secretary-General and humanitarian organizations by granting a full 12-month mandate.
messages.Brazil: Brazil thanks the Russian delegation for positively responding to our constructive proposals, particularly by restoring the agreed compromise formula from resolution 2585 (2021) and removing divisive elements. This balanced draft ensures the uninterrupted delivery of life-saving humanitarian assistance through Bab al-Hawa while promoting cross-line operations and vital early recovery projects. We urge all Council members to support this text in a spirit of consensus so as to maintain the humanitarian lifeline for the Syrian people.
messages.China: China appreciates the penholder's efforts and fully supports this balanced draft resolution, which respects the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. We welcome the emphasis on transitioning toward cross-line operations, the expansion of early recovery projects including basic electricity infrastructure, and the pragmatic six-month framework. China stands ready to vote in favour of this text and encourages all Council members to do the same.
messages.France: France acknowledges the deletion of previous unacceptable provisions, but the current draft remains fundamentally inadequate. The Secretary-General, OCHA, and humanitarian partners have stated unequivocally that a full 12-month renewal is a vital necessity to avoid an unmanageable humanitarian cliff-edge in the dead of winter. We cannot support a truncated or conditional renewal that leaves over four million vulnerable civilians hostage to political uncertainty.
messages.Gabon: Gabon welcomes the penholder's constructive engagement and the full incorporation of our proposed adjustments, notably by aligning the renewal mechanism with the formula in resolution 2585 (2021) and removing divisive elements. We believe this revised text provides a balanced, realistic, and humanitarian-centered basis to maintain vital cross-border access while bolstering early recovery and cross-line assistance. We urge all Council members to rally behind this compromise text to preserve Council unity and ensure the continuous delivery of aid to the Syrian population.
messages.Ghana: Ghana appreciates the penholder's efforts to bridge differences by drawing upon the language of resolution 2585 (2021) and removing contentious elements. However, we continue to stress that a straightforward 12-month extension is vital to guarantee operational predictability and uninterrupted life-saving aid for millions of vulnerable civilians, especially ahead of the winter season. We strongly encourage all Council members to demonstrate flexibility and work towards a consensus text that prioritizes purely humanitarian imperatives.
messages.India: India thanks the Russian delegation for incorporating our key proposals into this revision, particularly by aligning the renewal framework in operative paragraph 1 with resolution 2585 (2021) and emphasizing non-politicization in humanitarian support. We believe this revised draft strikes a constructive balance by securing vital humanitarian access through both cross-border and cross-line modalities while advancing early recovery projects across Syria. India fully supports the adoption of this text to maintain humanitarian operations without disruption.
messages.Ireland: Ireland appreciates the penholder's constructive removal of the reference to unilateral coercive measures and redundant reporting provisions. However, as co-penholder on this humanitarian file, we reiterate that a straightforward 12-month renewal is essential to provide humanitarian agencies with the planning certainty required to save lives, especially ahead of the harsh winter months. We urge the penholder to bridge this critical gap so that the Council can unite behind an operational, predictable mandate for north-west Syria.
messages.Kenya: Kenya appreciates the penholder's constructive adjustments to remove divisive language and align the draft closer to the consensus framework of resolution 2585 (2021). However, we reiterate that a predictable 12-month mandate is essential for humanitarian organizations to plan procurement, logistics, and life-saving operations ahead of the harsh winter season. We strongly urge all Council members to bridge remaining differences and maintain unity to ensure uninterrupted humanitarian access for the millions of Syrian people in need.
messages.Mexico: Mexico welcomes the constructive revisions made by the penholder, particularly the removal of contentious political language and the alignment of the text with the 6+6 reporting mechanism established in resolution 2585 (2021). Nevertheless, our principled position remains that humanitarian agencies require the certainty and predictability of a full, unconditional 12-month renewal to effectively plan and execute life-saving operations. We urge the penholder and Council members to prioritize the acute humanitarian needs of the Syrian civilian population above all political considerations.
messages.Norway: As humanitarian co-penholder alongside Ireland, Norway underscores that a full 12-month renewal of the cross-border mechanism is an operational and humanitarian necessity. Humanitarian partners and millions of vulnerable civilians cannot be subjected to a cliffhanger in the middle of winter, which would severely disrupt planning and life-saving logistics. We appreciate the penholder's adjustments, but we cannot support a text that fails to provide the certainty of a 12-month mandate.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates thanks the Russian delegation for accommodating our proposals in this revision, particularly by aligning the renewal mechanism with the consensus framework of resolution 2585 (2021) and emphasizing the critical importance of early recovery projects and cross-line delivery. This balanced text addresses the urgent humanitarian needs of the Syrian people while respecting the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria. We urge all Council members to support this compromise to ensure the uninterrupted flow of humanitarian assistance.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom notes the removal of references to unilateral coercive measures, but we cannot accept a text that fails to provide a guaranteed 12-month mandate. A six-month authorization expiring in the depths of winter jeopardizes planning and the delivery of life-saving humanitarian aid to over four million vulnerable Syrians. Only an unequivocal 12-month renewal based on United Nations humanitarian assessments will meet the critical needs on the ground.
messages.United States of America: The United States maintains that an unconditional, straightforward 12-month reauthorization is an absolute humanitarian imperative, echoing the clear call of the Secretary-General, UN agencies, and humanitarian NGOs on the ground. A six-month authorization expiring in January in the dead of winter creates unconscionable operational disruption and uncertainty for over four million vulnerable Syrians who rely on this lifeline. We cannot support any text that fails to secure a predictable, 12-month mandate.

reasons.Albania: While Albania strongly supports the cross-border humanitarian mechanism, it abstains on the Russian-drafted resolution in solidarity with humanitarian co-penholders and partners, reflecting its position alongside other elected members rather than supporting a competing text.
reasons.Brazil: Brazil supports maintaining the cross-border humanitarian mechanism through Bab al-Hawa alongside expanding cross-line aid and early recovery projects to address the critical needs of the Syrian people. Consistent with our stance during negotiations, Brazil votes in favour of the draft resolution.
reasons.China: China consistently supports initiatives that respect Syrian sovereignty, promote early recovery projects, and encourage cross-line humanitarian assistance, aligning with our strategic partnership with the Russian Federation. Following standard Security Council practice, our delegation reserves its remarks for an explanation of vote after the ballot.
reasons.France: France opposes this Russian-drafted text as it bypasses the humanitarian co-penholders (Ireland and Norway) and incorporates problematic language regarding early recovery, electricity, and regime-dictated conditions. Aligned with the United States and the United Kingdom, France votes against the draft resolution.
reasons.Gabon: Gabon supported the draft resolution during negotiations as it preserves the vital Bab al-Hawa humanitarian corridor and supports early recovery projects for the Syrian people.
reasons.Ghana: Ghana votes in favour because our primary request for a predictable 12-month extension of the humanitarian cross-border mechanism at Bab al-Hawa has been directly incorporated into the draft resolution.
reasons.India: India supports the extension of the humanitarian mechanism alongside the emphasis on early recovery projects, cross-line deliveries, and non-politicized humanitarian aid to the Syrian people, consistent with its established stance. India typically delivers its explanation of vote after the voting procedure is concluded.
reasons.Ireland: Ireland's foremost humanitarian priority as co-penholder on the Syria humanitarian file is securing an uninterrupted 12-month mandate for the cross-border mechanism at Bab al-Hawa. As the penholder accepted Ireland's red line by granting a full twelve-month extension until 10 July 2023, Ireland votes in favour to protect this vital lifeline for millions of civilians in north-west Syria.
reasons.Kenya: Kenya strongly supports the uninterrupted delivery of humanitarian assistance to the Syrian people across all modalities, and our key proposal for a 12-month extension to ensure predictability and planning for humanitarian operations was fully incorporated into the draft text.
reasons.Mexico: Mexico votes in favour because the draft resolution incorporates our primary objective of securing a full twelve-month renewal for the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism, ensuring operational predictability and uninterrupted humanitarian aid delivery to millions of civilians in Syria.
reasons.Norway: Norway's primary humanitarian objective as co-penholder—securing a 12-month extension of the cross-border aid mechanism at Bab al-Hawa—has been incorporated into the draft resolution, fulfilling our essential conditions to ensure predictable, life-saving assistance to millions in north-west Syria.
reasons.Russian Federation: As the sponsor and author of this draft resolution, the Russian Federation naturally votes in favour of its own text, which provides a balanced and workable framework for humanitarian assistance in Syria while respecting Syrian sovereignty.
reasons.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates supports the draft resolution as it ensures the continuity of vital humanitarian assistance to the Syrian people, respects Syrian sovereignty, and places appropriate emphasis on early recovery projects and expanding cross-line aid deliveries.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom opposes this competing text submitted by the Russian Federation, which undermines the established process led by the humanitarian co-penholders (Ireland and Norway) and fails to adequately protect principled, independent humanitarian assistance. In coordination with our allies, the UK votes against the draft resolution.
reasons.United States of America: The United States cannot support a draft resolution put forward by the Russian Federation that sidelines the humanitarian co-penholders and seeks to dictate terms on humanitarian access, early recovery, and cross-line delivery that undermine principled aid operations. In line with our stated opposition and coordinated P3 position, the United States votes against the draft resolution.

after.Albania:
Albania is deeply concerned by the situation in Syria, where over a decade of conflict has caused immense suffering and left millions of people in dire need of humanitarian assistance to survive. The cross-border humanitarian mechanism through Bab al-Hawa remains an indispensable lifeline for over four million people in north-west Syria, the vast majority of whom are women and children. 

Albania has consistently maintained that humanitarian aid must never be politicized, instrumentalized, or held hostage to political agendas. The delivery of assistance must be guided strictly by humanitarian principles—humanity, neutrality, impartiality, and independence—and determined by the actual needs on the ground.

While we recognize the importance of expanding cross-line operations and supporting early recovery projects consistent with international law, cross-line assistance cannot, at this stage, substitute for the scale and scope of the cross-border mechanism. The humanitarian community requires predictability, stability, and transparency to plan and execute life-saving operations effectively.

For these reasons, Albania could not support a text that does not sufficiently meet the urgent, well-documented humanitarian requirements on the ground or command the necessary consensus among Council members. We decided to abstain, emphasizing once again that the Council’s primary duty must be to ensure the unhindered flow of life-saving aid to all civilians in need across Syria.

We urge all Council members to redouble efforts to find common ground and ensure that the vital lifeline to the Syrian people is not severed. We also reaffirm our full support for a Syrian-led, Syrian-owned political process in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015), which remains the only viable path to lasting peace in Syria.
after.Brazil:
Mr. President,

Brazil voted in favour of the draft resolution because we firmly believe that the humanitarian imperative must guide our actions above all other considerations. 

The humanitarian situation in Syria remains dire, with more than 4 million people in the north-west depending directly on the aid delivered through the cross-border mechanism to survive. For Brazil, preserving this vital humanitarian lifeline is essential. At the same time, we have consistently underscored the need to expand cross-line deliveries to all parts of Syria, in full respect for the guiding principles of humanitarian emergency assistance and the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic.

We also welcome the emphasis placed on early recovery projects. Humanitarian aid cannot be confined solely to emergency relief; restoring access to water, electricity, sanitation, health, education, and shelter is indispensable to building resilience and creating conditions for the dignified and voluntary return of displaced persons and refugees.

Brazil deeply regrets that the Security Council has once again failed to reach consensus on such a critical matter, directly affecting the lives of millions of vulnerable civilians. The expiration of the mandate of resolution 2585 (2021) is fast approaching, and Syrian civilians cannot afford an impasse in this Council. 

We urge all Council members to remain engaged in constructive dialogue, overcome political divergences, and work tirelessly in the coming days to find a viable compromise that ensures the uninterrupted delivery of humanitarian assistance to all those in need across Syria.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.China:
*(spoke in Chinese)*

China regrets that the draft resolution just voted on was not adopted.

China has always attached great importance to the humanitarian situation in Syria and supports the United Nations and the international community in providing humanitarian assistance to the Syrian people in accordance with the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence. At the same time, we have consistently maintained that humanitarian operations must fully respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria, as well as the ownership of the Syrian Government.

The cross-border humanitarian mechanism is a temporary arrangement made under special circumstances. With the development of the situation on the ground, cross-line delivery should become the main channel for humanitarian assistance to Syria. The draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation took into full consideration the concerns of all parties, promoted cross-line assistance, expanded early recovery projects, and provided for the continuation of humanitarian assistance through the Bab al-Hawa crossing. The draft resolution received the support of the vast majority of Council members, and China voted in favour. We express deep regret over the negative votes cast by certain permanent members.

China wishes to emphasize once again that early recovery projects are vital to helping the Syrian people rebuild their lives, restore basic infrastructure, and create conditions for the safe and dignified return of refugees and displaced persons. The international community should scale up investment in early recovery across all parts of Syria without political strings attached.

Furthermore, unilateral coercive measures imposed on Syria have for years severely undermined Syria’s economic and social development, impeded the delivery of humanitarian supplies, and aggravated the suffering of the Syrian people. Such illegal sanctions run counter to the efforts of the Council and the international community to improve the humanitarian situation, and must be completely and unconditionally lifted without delay.

The mandate of the humanitarian cross-border mechanism is about to expire. China calls on all members of the Council to uphold a constructive and cooperative attitude, demonstrate flexibility, avoid politicizing humanitarian issues, and continue consultations so as to find a proper solution acceptable to all parties.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.France:
France voted against the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation.

Having just isolated itself by vetoing the balanced compromise text prepared by the co-penholders, Ireland and Norway—a text supported by the vast majority of the members of this Council and by the humanitarian community—the Russian Federation has attempted to force through a draft that does not adequately address the desperate needs of the Syrian people.

Today, more than 4 million people in north-west Syria depend on cross-border assistance delivered through the Bab al-Hawa crossing for their survival. As the Secretary-General, United Nations agencies, and non-governmental organizations on the ground have stated repeatedly, there is currently no viable alternative to this vital lifeline. A predictable and secure framework of 12 months is essential to enable humanitarian actors to plan their operations, preposition aid, and ensure uninterrupted relief, particularly with winter approaching. 

We cannot accept a mechanism that keeps millions of civilians in perpetual uncertainty, nor can we allow vital humanitarian access to be held hostage to political bargaining and blackmail. 

France and the European Union will continue to support the Syrian people and fund humanitarian action, including early recovery projects, in full accordance with humanitarian principles of independence, neutrality, and impartiality. However, humanitarian assistance must never be instrumentalized by the Syrian regime, nor diverted for political ends.

France calls on all members of the Council to show responsibility and ensure that cross-border assistance is preserved in order to prevent a catastrophe for millions of vulnerable Syrians.
after.India:
Mr. President,

I take the floor to explain India’s vote on the draft resolution that has just been considered by the Council.

India voted in favour of the draft resolution. We have consistently emphasized the urgent need for scaled-up, effective, and non-politicized humanitarian assistance to all Syrians across the country, without discrimination or preconditions. Over a decade of conflict and terrorism has caused immense suffering to the Syrian people, and millions remain in dire need of basic sustenance and essential services. 

India has always maintained that humanitarian assistance must be guided by the United Nations guiding principles of humanitarian emergency assistance, with full respect for the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. While the cross-border mechanism was established as a temporary measure to address extraordinary circumstances, all modalities of aid delivery—including cross-line assistance—must be actively pursued, strengthened, and expanded across all parts of Syria. 

We also welcome the emphasis placed on early recovery projects. Humanitarian aid cannot be confined solely to immediate emergency relief; it is vital that support be extended to basic infrastructure and essential services, including water, sanitation, health, education, electricity, and shelter, which are crucial for creating conditions conducive to the safe, dignified, and voluntary return of displaced persons.

India regrets that the Council was unable to reach consensus on this critical humanitarian issue today. At a time when the humanitarian needs of the Syrian people are acute, the politicization of the humanitarian track only compounds their suffering. We urge all members of the Council to bridge differences and engage constructively to ensure that the vital lifeline of humanitarian assistance to the people of Syria is not disrupted.

I thank you.
after.Ireland:
Ireland, together with Norway, as co-penholders on the Syrian humanitarian dossier, has consistently approached this critical file with a single, clear objective: to ensure that life-saving humanitarian assistance continues to reach all Syrians in need, wherever they are, and by all available modalities.

Our vote in favour of the draft resolution today was guided solely by this humanitarian imperative. Over four million people in north-west Syria depend on cross-border humanitarian assistance for their basic survival. For them, the Bab al-Hawa crossing is not a political talking point; it is an irreplaceable lifeline. A twelve-month renewal provides the necessary certainty, stability, and operational predictability that the United Nations and humanitarian partners require to plan and deliver vital relief efficiently and effectively.

We deeply regret that the Council has not been able to adopt this resolution today. With the current mandate set to expire in just two days, the Security Council cannot afford to walk away from its responsibilities to the Syrian people. Failure to maintain cross-border access would have catastrophic consequences for millions of vulnerable men, women, and children who have already endured more than a decade of conflict, displacement, and immense suffering.

Ireland remains firmly committed to exhausting every diplomatic avenue. We urge all Council members to put the humanitarian needs of the Syrian people first and to work constructively with us and Norway over the coming hours to find a consensus that preserves this vital humanitarian lifeline.
after.Mexico:
(spoke in Spanish):

Mexico voted in favour of the draft resolution just considered by the Security Council because our priority has always been, and will continue to be, responding to the urgent humanitarian needs of the Syrian civilian population.

More than 4 million people in north-western Syria depend on the humanitarian assistance delivered through the Bab Al-Hawa border crossing. Humanitarian organizations on the ground and the Secretary-General himself have repeatedly emphasized that a 12-month extension is indispensable to provide operational certainty, predictability, and adequate planning for life-saving relief efforts. It was for this fundamental reason that Mexico cast a vote in favour. 

At the same time, Mexico has consistently maintained that all modalities of humanitarian assistance—both cross-border and cross-line—are essential and complementary. We also recognize the critical importance of early recovery projects in water, sanitation, health, and education to alleviate the suffering of the population and create basic conditions for dignity and resilience.

Mexico deeply regrets that the Council was unable to adopt this resolution and that political considerations have once again prevented us from reaching a consensus on an exclusively humanitarian matter. The Security Council cannot remain paralyzed while the lives and wellbeing of millions of vulnerable people hang in the balance.

With the current mandate set to expire in just two days, Mexico urges all members of the Security Council to set aside political differences and redouble dialogue and diplomatic efforts in the hours ahead to find a compromise that ensures the uninterrupted delivery of humanitarian aid to all those who need it in Syria.
after.Norway:
Norway voted in favour of the draft resolution. 

As co-penholder with Ireland on the Syrian humanitarian file, Norway has worked tirelessly and constructively over the past months with all members of the Security Council to find common ground and ensure that the vital cross-border humanitarian mechanism is renewed. 

We deeply regret that the Council was unable to adopt this resolution today. For Norway, the priority has always been and remains singularly humanitarian: to ensure that life-saving aid continues to reach the more than 4 million people in north-west Syria who depend on it for their daily survival. The humanitarian needs on the ground are at their highest levels since the start of the conflict, and as the Secretary-General, United Nations agencies, and humanitarian partners have repeatedly emphasized, cross-border aid remains an indispensable and irreplaceable lifeline. 

We voted in favour because we believe that a 12-month renewal provides the predictability, stability, and operational certainty that humanitarian actors require to plan and deliver life-saving operations, including early recovery projects. We also remain fully committed to supporting the expansion of cross-line deliveries and early recovery initiatives across all parts of Syria, in line with humanitarian principles. 

With the current mandate expiring in just two days, on 10 July, the Security Council cannot turn its back on the Syrian people. We have a collective responsibility under the Charter to act. Together with Ireland, Norway will continue to engage with all Council members in the hours and days ahead to redouble our efforts and find a way forward that secures this critical lifeline for those most in need.
after.Russian Federation:
We regret that the draft resolution that we submitted today has been blocked by the negative votes of the three Western permanent members — the United States, the United Kingdom, and France.

Today’s vote has clearly exposed who is genuinely interested in delivering humanitarian assistance to the people of Syria and who continues to use humanitarian issues solely for narrow political gains and geopolitical games. Eleven members of the Security Council supported our draft resolution, which confirms that our approach was balanced, viable, and aimed at addressing the real needs of ordinary Syrians throughout the entire country without discrimination.

Our text offered a constructive and forward-looking solution. It not only provided for extending the operation of the Bab al-Hawa crossing, but also placed vital emphasis on expanding cross-line deliveries and supporting early recovery projects, including the restoration of water, health, sanitation, education, and basic electricity infrastructure. These early recovery efforts are essential to allow Syrians to rebuild their lives and create conditions for refugees and internally displaced persons to return to their homes in dignity and safety.

Yet the Western troika has once again demonstrated total disregard for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic and for the guiding principles of humanitarian emergency assistance set out in General Assembly resolution 46/182. They remain stubbornly focused on preserving an anachronistic, non-transparent cross-border mechanism that circumvents the legitimate authorities in Damascus and feeds terrorists in Idlib, while actively starving the rest of the Syrian people through inhumane unilateral coercive measures and sanctions.

By vetoing our draft, the Western permanent members have assumed full responsibility for any potential disruption of humanitarian deliveries to the Syrian population. The Russian Federation remains committed to supporting the Syrian people and upholding the principles of the United Nations Charter, and we will continue our principled efforts to ensure that assistance reaches all Syrians in need without political conditionalities.
after.United Arab Emirates:
(spoke in Arabic): The United Arab Emirates voted in favour of the draft resolution, guided by our firm conviction that humanitarian assistance must remain purely humanitarian and shielded from political considerations. The primary objective of the Security Council today must be to alleviate the immense suffering of the Syrian people and ensure that vital aid continues to reach all those in need across Syria, without disruption or politicization.

Our position has always been clear and consistent: addressing the dire humanitarian crisis in Syria requires a pragmatic and comprehensive approach. This includes utilizing all available modalities—both cross-border and cross-line mechanisms—and expanding cross-line operations to all parts of the country. At the same time, we place great importance on early recovery projects, particularly in essential sectors such as water, sanitation, health, education, and electricity, which are crucial for restoring basic livelihoods, building resilience, and creating conditions conducive to the safe, dignified, and voluntary return of refugees and displaced persons.

We deeply regret that the Council was unable to reach consensus today on this critical file. Millions of Syrian civilians rely on this Council to set aside political differences and prioritize their basic humanitarian needs. We therefore urge all Council members to continue constructive and flexible negotiations in the coming hours, before the expiration of the mandate, to bridge differences and arrive at a consensus that serves the humanitarian interests of the brotherly Syrian people, while upholding the sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity of Syria.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
The United Kingdom voted against this draft resolution. 

Over 4 million people in north-west Syria depend on United Nations cross-border humanitarian aid for their survival. For months, the United Nations Secretary-General, humanitarian agencies, and non-governmental organizations on the ground have been unequivocal: a predictable, reliable 12-month mandate is essential to plan life-saving operations, maintain supply chains, and deliver food, shelter, and medical care to millions of vulnerable civilians.

Earlier today, the Council saw a carefully balanced, compromise text put forward by the co-penholders, Ireland and Norway—a text that reflected weeks of intensive consultations and had the overwhelming support of Council members. That text was vetoed by Russia. 

Instead of working collaboratively to meet the urgent needs of the Syrian people, Russia has sought to force a divisive approach that fails to provide the necessary humanitarian certainty and ignores the clear operational realities described by the United Nations. The United Kingdom cannot endorse a text that undermines the principled delivery of aid and plays politics with the lives of millions of innocent Syrians.

Let me be clear: the United Kingdom fully supports delivering assistance through all modalities, including cross-line operations, and we support early recovery projects in line with international humanitarian principles. But cross-line aid cannot substitute for the scale and scope of the cross-border operation at Bab al-Hawa. 

The Security Council has a responsibility to protect vulnerable civilians, not leave them hostage to political maneuvering. With the mandate expiring in just two days, we urge all Council members to support the co-penholders and work constructively to find a solution that ensures life-saving assistance continues to reach those who desperately need it.
after.United States of America:
I thank you, Mr. President.

Today is a dark day in the Security Council. Just moments ago, Russia cast a veto against a compromise text, drafted by Ireland and Norway, that was supported by the vast majority of the members of this Council, by the Secretary-General, and by every single humanitarian agency operating on the ground in Syria. 

And now, Russia has forced a vote on its own text—an ultimatum designed not to save Syrian lives, but to play cynical political games with the fate of millions of desperate people. The United States voted "no" on this draft resolution. 

Let us be completely clear about what was at stake. More than four million Syrians in north-west Syria depend on the United Nations cross-border humanitarian mechanism for their survival—for food, for clean water, for shelter, and for critical medicine. Humanitarians have told us repeatedly and unequivocally that a six-month mandate is unworkable. A six-month authorization would mean this lifeline would expire in January, in the dead of winter, when the cold is biting, when roads are impassable, and when humanitarian needs are at their peak. It would leave aid organizations unable to plan, procure, or pre-position supplies, throwing life-saving operations into chaos. 

A six-month authorization is not a compromise; it is an eviction notice for aid agencies in the depths of winter. It forces the Council to renegotiate this vital lifeline in six months under the threat of another Russian veto. We could not, in good conscience, support a draft that holds the lives of Syrian men, women, and children hostage to Moscow’s political maneuvering.

The United States has consistently supported delivering aid by all modalities—both cross-border and cross-line. We have supported early recovery projects consistent with resolution 2585 (2021). But cross-line assistance cannot replace the scale and scope of the cross-border operation at Bab al-Hawa. 

Russia’s actions today have brought this Council to the brink of cutting off life-saving assistance to millions of people. It is a callous display of disregard for human life and international humanitarian principles. 

The mandate expires in two days, on July 10. The United States remains committed to finding a solution. We urge all Council members to put humanity first, put politics aside, and keep this vital lifeline open. The Syrian people are counting on us, and we must not fail them.

Thank you, Mr. President.
